paper.title: LUCID: Latent-Skill Unified Control via Imagined Dynamics for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-08-07; latest public version verified 2026-08-30. decision_relevance.why_admitted: LUCID supplies a current, source-located example of a state-based phase oracle turning demonstrations into a structured skill interface, a staged task reward, and learned closed-loop skill composition over a frozen low-level controller; its coupled training stack also defines a precise fixed-trainer boundary for Sam's experiments.
not_evidence_for: automatic discovery, ranking, splicing, or verification of reference motions
an oracle-only or task-reward-only intervention under a fixed trainer
VIBE integration or a frozen foundation whole-body tracker
vision-based control, real-robot transfer, or cross-embodiment generality
availability of reproducible code, checkpoints, or full supplementary details

mechanisms.name: Oracle-labeled structured latent interface
mechanisms.description: During LLC training, a state-and-goal oracle assigns the current interaction phase. Its one-hot semantic anchor is concatenated with Gaussian within-skill variation and normalized; after training, the HLC selects the resulting structured latent.

mechanisms.name: Interaction-aware LLC curriculum
mechanisms.description: The LLC warm-starts through carry, rearrangement, and retreat-and-chaining stages. Only the goal-conditioned task reward and reference-state initialization change between stages, coupling reward design to the sampled starting-state distribution.

mechanisms.name: Frozen structured-latent low-level controller
mechanisms.description: An ASE-derived PPO controller maps proprioceptive, object, task-guidance, and structured-latent inputs to joint-level PD targets; it is frozen before HLC/world-model learning.

mechanisms.name: Skill-level macro-dynamics world model
mechanisms.description: Given compact task state plus a structured skill latent and guidance command, separate heads predict residual continuous-state change, binary task-progress flags, and continuation probability after the frozen LLC executes one macro action.

mechanisms.name: High-level skill policy trained in imagination
mechanisms.description: A goal-conditioned actor-critic starts short imagined rollouts from real replay states, optimizes task-progress returns discounted by predicted continuation, and alternates with simulator collection and world-model updates.

mechanisms.name: Annealed geometry-oracle warm start
mechanisms.description: The categorical HLC action is initially behavior-cloned from geometry-oracle labels in replay; the coefficient decays to zero, so the oracle initializes exploration rather than fixing the final skill sequence.

failure_modes.name: Privileged-state dependence
failure_modes.description: The policy and world model use simulator state; visual control is left to future work.

failure_modes.name: Limited task, object, and embodiment diversity
failure_modes.description: Evidence comes from one 15-body, 28-joint simulated humanoid and HITR-derived rearrangement tasks; broader tasks and real transfer are untested.

failure_modes.name: Success decays with chain length
failure_modes.description: The authors report roughly 56% prefix success at three objects and 21% at five objects despite more graceful degradation than baselines.

failure_modes.name: Favorable baseline handoff resets
failure_modes.description: Baseline adapters reset only the humanoid to a favorable pose at each subtask handoff; success/placement comparisons favor baselines, while completion time is not directly comparable.

failure_modes.name: Dense shaping reduces OOD success
failure_modes.description: Dense LUCID obtains 50.2% OOD SR2 versus 63.1% for sparse LUCID, a 12.9-point drop.

failure_modes.name: Coupled system changes violate fixed-trainer isolation
failure_modes.description: LUCID modifies and trains the LLC interface, curricula, RSI, rewards, HLC, world model, replay, and optimizer schedule; its gains cannot be attributed to Sam's oracle or task-reward knob alone.

failure_modes.name: Missing public implementation and supplement
failure_modes.description: The nine-page v1 repeatedly cites supplementary sections that are absent from its source package, and the record exposes no paper-specific code, checkpoints, project, or data release.

evaluation.name: Shared ID/OOD two-object comparison
evaluation.description: Across 62 ID and 20 OOD tasks, LUCID reports SR2 of 73.4% and 68.4%, versus 39.8% and 37.0% for the strongest mean baseline; placement error is also lowest.

evaluation.name: World-model and reward-density ablation
evaluation.description: World-model variants beat model-free HLCs in all four ID/OOD by sparse/dense SR2 comparisons; dense shaping has little ID benefit and lower OOD transfer.

evaluation.name: Structured versus unstructured latent ablation
evaluation.description: Structured pairs report 74.2% ID and 66.4% OOD SR2, while unstructured pairs report 0% SR2 on both; both interfaces remain command-decodable, so task alignment rather than decodability alone is implicated.

evaluation.name: Three-to-five-object prefix-success extension
evaluation.description: LUCID is evaluated beyond its two-object training chain and reports about 56% SR3 and 21% SR5; exact plotted values beyond the prose approximations are not tabulated.

evidence.claim: arXiv v1 was submitted on 7 August 2026 and remained the only public version when verified on 30 August 2026.

evidence.locator: Figure 1 and Section 4 Method, opening paragraph
evidence.claim: LUCID trains an ASE-derived latent-conditioned LLC, freezes it, then jointly trains a goal-conditioned HLC and macro-dynamics world model.
The LLC objective combines adversarial imitation and goal-conditioned task reward; the state-and-goal oracle selects the current phase skill.
Each semantic skill receives a one-hot anchor and remaining latent dimensions encode Gaussian within-skill variation; the HLC selects this latent after LLC freezing.
The three LLC stages are carry, rearrangement, and retreat-and-chaining; only task reward and reference-state initialization change between stages.
One macro action contains structured latent plus guidance; after frozen-LLC execution, the world model predicts residual continuous state, binary flags, and continuation.
Training alternates real simulator collection, replay-based world-model updates, and short imagined actor-critic rollouts started from real replay states.
A geometry-based oracle behavior-clones the categorical HLC component early; its coefficient is annealed to zero and oracle labels are used only while that coefficient is positive.
The benchmark has 62 ID training tasks, 20 OOD tasks, standard two-object chains, an extension through five objects, and OMOMO/SAMP reference motions for LLC training.

The paper specifies 0.2 m placement success, three seeds, a 15-body/28-joint humanoid, 60 Hz simulation, 30 Hz LLC, 20-step macro actions, 12-step imagination, sequence 32, batch 64, 8192 environments, and two RTX 4090s for LLC training.
LUCID reports 73.4% ID and 68.4% OOD SR2 with 0.32 m and 0.52 m APE, outperforming the compared baseline means.

evidence.locator: Section 5.3.3 Extended multi-objects tasks and Figure 3
evidence.claim: In prose, the authors report approximately 56% SR3 and 21% SR5; exact longer-chain values are not tabulated.

evidence.locator: Table 2 and Section 5.4.1 On world model effectiveness
evidence.claim: World-model variants outperform model-free HLCs in all sparse/dense ID/OOD SR2 cells, while dense LUCID OOD SR2 is 12.9 points below sparse LUCID.

evidence.locator: Figure 6, Table 3, and Section 5.4.2 On structured latent interface
evidence.claim: Structured LLC/HLC pairs achieve 74.2% ID and 66.4% OOD SR2 versus zero SR2 for unstructured pairs; three structured commands and no unstructured command exceed the 0.4 sustained-lift threshold.
The authors identify privileged state and limited task, object, and embodiment diversity; vision and real-world transfer remain future work.
Baseline adapters reset the humanoid to a favorable pose at each handoff, so success/APE comparisons favor baselines and completion times are not directly comparable.
